subject: Lancer-4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — mitigation applied and next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Ella Park <ella.p@stromalabs.com>, ops@stromalabs.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: [Action Required] Lancer-4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — mitigation plan

Hi Ella / Stroma ops team,

I'm reaching out because we're seeing an elevated rate of 5xx responses and timeouts for requests routed to the Lancer-4b family starting ~08:50 PDT. The spike appears concentrated on sequences between 1k-4k tokens and correlates with a kernel selection path that degrades under sustained concurrency. Impact so far: ~12% of requests returning 5xx over the last 20 minutes (your tenant: ~18% of your traffic routed to Lancer-4b).

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Applied traffic isolation to prevent cross-tenant saturation for Lancer-4b hosts.
- Implemented a short-term routing rule to prefer the compatible fallback model (Lancer-3b-compat) for requests with >1000 tokens — this is live as of 09:05 PDT.
- Kicked off deeper triage with runtime engineers; Marcus is on the kernel selection traces.

Attachments: short error snippets + a quick metrics snapshot (see attached).

Ask: Can you confirm whether you can tolerate short-term routing to Lancer-3b-compat for long-context requests? If yes, we'll keep the routing in place until we validate the kernel fix. If no, we'll roll back but will need to throttle burst concurrency to limit 5xx risk.

I'll follow up with a triage summary and ETA once Marcus has an RCA.

— Camila

Hi Ella — thank you for the quick reply.

Per Ben's recommendation we've routed long-context requests away from Lancer-4b and onto Lancer-3b-compat at 09:05 PDT. Early telemetry shows a ~40% reduction in 5xx rate for your tenant and timeouts are decreasing, though a small tail remains. I've attached the short-term metrics snapshot.

What to expect next:
- Marcus will continue deep triage to identify the kernel selector regression and produce an RCA.
- If Marcus' fix affects runtime binary/kernels we will schedule a controlled rollout starting in the next 6–12 hours with canary and quick rollback.
- We'll keep the fallback routing in place until canary validates stability.

If the temporary routing causes any user-facing latency issues for you, we can revert, but that will likely increase 5xx exposure. We can also apply a narrower routing rule (only for requests >2k tokens) if you'd prefer less change.

Please confirm whether the fallback routing is acceptable; if you OK it, we'll leave it in place and provide hourly telemetry.

Thanks — Camila

Subject: Lancer-4b incident closure & RCA summary

Ella — summary and next steps now that we've stabilized traffic: thank you again for the quick coordination.

What we found (high level):
- Root cause: a regression in the kernel-selection heuristic introduced in runtime v2.11.0 that selects an attention kernel variant which under high concurrency and mid-length sequences (1k–4k tokens) caused excessive memory pressure and failed inference calls (5xx).
- Why it manifested now: an uptick in long-context usage plus a narrow sequence-length distribution in your traffic amplified the failure mode.

What we did:
- Short-term: routed long-context requests to Lancer-3b-compat and isolated affected Lancer-4b hosts (09:05 PDT, Jun 12). This reduced 5xx by ~40% for your tenant within 30 minutes.
- Mid-term: rolled back the kernel-selection change from v2.11.0 to v2.10.4 on the Lancer-4b fleet under a canary (completed 13:00 PDT, Jun 13). Canary validation (6k requests) shows no regressions.
- Long-term: pushing a follow-up runtime patch that adds a safety check on kernel selection for high-concurrency long-sequence requests; ETA for global rollout: 48–72 hours pending QA.

Customer impact & remediation offer:
- Observed peak incident window: Jun 12 08:50–13:00 PDT (your tenant saw most errors in the 09:00–10:15 window).
- We're offering a one-time account credit equivalent to estimated overage/error cost; Neha, please coordinate the credit amount with Stroma Finance (Ella flagged needing this documented against DL-83721).

Open items:
- Ella: confirm whether the narrower routing (>2k tokens) is preferred; we can leave it that way during rollout.
- Neha: coordinate a formal credit note for Stroma (send draft to Ella).
- Markus: follow up with runtime PR link and timeline for the safety-check rollout; include test coverage notes.

I'll keep this thread for coordination; we'll close the incident once Ella confirms the experience is stable.

— Camila
